confirmed.statement: S1-O1 through S1-O4: two independent graduate researchers in creativity rated generated ideas on 7-point novelty and usefulness scales, blind to condition and identity; ratings were averaged across raters and each participant's ideas, supporting expert_raters and participant units.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 13, section 2.5; p. 14, section 2.6; codebook section 6.

confirmed.statement: S1-O5 through S1-O8: fluency counts valid ideas per individual, and flexibility counts categories within that individual's ideas; two additional creativity researchers coded categories, supporting category_count, participant units, and flexibility rather than diversity.

S1-O9 through S1-O12: immediate and delayed perspective taking are coded category matches to the partner's preceding ideas, aggregated into participant proportions; they are distinct from the self-reported partner-perspective-taking questionnaire.

S1-O9 through S1-O14: other/with_ai is supported for these interaction-process measures; HAI comparisons involve a human and AI, and forward flow uses the shared dyad history, rather than comparing different AI-assisted people's outputs.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 13-14, section 2.5; p. 39, Supplementary Figure 1 caption; codebook sections 1 and 6.

confirmed.statement: All 14 outcomes concern the same AUT/PIT output generated during human-AI turn taking, supporting AI availability and immediate timing; delayed perspective taking means matching an earlier turn, not a later task after AI removal.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 9-10, sections 2.2-2.3; pp. 13-14, section 2.5; p. 39, Supplementary Figure 1; pp. 42-43, Appendix 1.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 through S1-O12 correctly distinguish participant-level human-role contrasts from explicitly labeled team-level contrasts including AI output; AUT table counts are 49 HAI and 53 HH dyads, and PIT counts are 54 HAI and 55 HH dyads.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 13-14, sections 2.5-2.6; p. 17, Table 2; p. 21, Table 4.

confirmed.statement: S1-O3: all AUT usefulness role pairs have ps > 0.05; dyad levels 4.60 (0.50) versus 4.79 (0.76), t(90.24) = -1.5, d = -0.3 and p > 0.05 match.
S1-O4: PIT usefulness p = 0.190 is correctly identified as the overall role comparison; dyad levels 4.98 (0.26) versus 5.07 (0.48), t(84.21) = -1.27, p = 0.208, d = -0.24 match.
S1-O5: all AUT fluency role pairs have ps > 0.05; dyad levels 22.51 (6.92) versus 19.38 (9.30), t(95.77) = 1.94, d = 0.38 and p > 0.05 match.
S1-O7: all AUT flexibility role pairs have ps > 0.05; dyad levels 7.68 (1.59) versus 7.26 (1.59), t(99.4) = 1.33, d = 0.26 and p > 0.05 match.
S1-O9: human AUT immediate perspective taking t(145.64) = 3.21, p = 0.005, d = 0.66; dyad levels 0.33 (0.18) versus 0.21 (0.13), t(86.45) = 3.93, p < 0.001, d = 0.78, all match.
S1-O10: AUT delayed perspective taking has no significant role differences; dyad levels 0.52(0.17) versus 0.45(0.15), t(96.25) = 2.30, p = 0.024, d = 0.46 match.

S1-O12: human PIT delayed perspective taking is nonsignificant in the results and described as marginal in the discussion; dyad levels 0.59 (0.13) versus 0.44 (0.15), t(105.19) = 5.55, p < 0.001, d = 1.06 match.

summary: The outcome coding was not refuted: all 14 outcomes are scored on generated ideas, and the classifications, qualified analysis units, and reported results are supported by the saved PDF. Criterion 3 holds because independent creativity researchers rated participants' ideas for novelty and usefulness.
